IBM Installation Manager should not be installed on an NFS mounted disk (or network-mounted drive such as your Ingram Server). According to IBM documentation, Installation Manager must only be installed on a local disk. Installing on NFS or remote drives causes issues including segmentation faults and path-related errors when the drive is mounted on different machines. Unmounting and remounting will not resolve this; you need to install Installation Manager on a local disk on each machine where it is needed.

The issue occurs because JARs in the WAS server's plugins directory use an exports list that specifies which classes can be called by user code. Classes not on this exports list are considered internal use only and will throw NoClassDefFoundError at runtime, even though they may appear available during compilation in RAD. To resolve this, either ensure the classes you call appear on the plugin JAR's exports list, or place the JAR in the server's library directory instead of the plugins directory, because the library directory uses a different class loader that does not implement the exports list restriction.

In db2diag.log corruption entries, look for the object identifier in the format Obj={pool:<tablespace_id>;obj:<object_id>;type:<type>}. Here, pool is the Tablespace ID, obj is the Object ID, and type indicates the object type (0 = Table Object, 1 = Index). To find the name of the corrupted object, run the following query against the catalog: db2 "select char(tabname,20), char(tabschema,20) from syscat.tables where tableid=<ObjectID> and tbspaceid=<TablespaceID>". For example, for Obj={pool:3;obj:21;type:0}, use: db2 "select char(tabname,20), char(tabschema,20) from syscat.tables where tableid=21 and tbspaceid=3".

The documentation does not specify the exact precision of the backside persistent timeout value. However, the 'Failed to process response headers' error is not solely determined by the timeout value comparison. According to the technote, this error almost always indicates a connection failure where the service did not receive any response headers or data. Classic causes include: (1) a slow response causing connection timeout before receiving the response, or (2) a failed connection attempt due to a closed persistent connection—for example, a reused connection that was already closed by something outside of DataPower (such as the backend device closing it at its 30-second timeout, or other network issues). Even with DataPower set to 28 seconds and the backend at 30 seconds, the error can occur if DataPower attempts to reuse a persistent connection that the backend has already closed, or due to network errors. A packet trace and debug-level logging are recommended to confirm the specific cause.

The use of the Client Channel Definition Table (CCDT) with XA connections is not supported. This restriction exists because of transaction recovery: if the application server stops while transactions are still active, there is no way to ensure it will connect to the same queue manager when it restarts, which can leave in-doubt transactions dangling and unresolved. When attempting to create an XA connection using a CCDT, you will receive error MQJMS1068: failed to obtain XAResource. To resolve this, do not use the CCDT-based connection factory (jms/QM) for XA transactions; use the direct connection factories (jms/QM01 and jms/QM02) instead.

On a 64-bit JVM using compressed references, Class Pointers and Monitors/Locks are stored using 32-bit pointers and must therefore be allocated in the low-memory region (the first 4GB of address space), even if the Java heap is located above 4GB. The OS memory allocator may exhaust this low-memory region even when the system has plenty of free memory overall, causing a Native OutOfMemory (NOOM). Additionally, an insufficient ulimit setting (nproc/-u on Linux, -r on AIX) restricting the number of threads per user can cause NOOM with 'Failed to create a thread' errors. To resolve, consider setting -Xgc:preferredHeapBase or -Xmx4G, using -Xmcrs to reserve low-memory space at startup (Java 6.0.16.3, 6.1.8.3, 7.0.8.10, 7.1.2.10 and later), reducing application Class Pointers and Monitors/Locks usage, or increasing the relevant ulimit values.

The segmentation error (GPF) occurs when the gtk libraries are installed but are not at the required versions. Even if you have the latest versions of the libraries listed in the technote, Installation Manager requires specific versions of the gtk libraries to function correctly on AIX. The core dump is generated because the SWT library (libswt-pi-gtk) cannot be loaded properly when the installed gtk libraries do not match the exact versions required by the Eclipse Rich Client Platform that Installation Manager is based on.

For IIB v10.0.0.9 and later, use the mqsichangeproperties command to generate a Java thread dump (javacore) against an execution group (Integration Server): mqsichangeproperties <Int.Node> -e <Int.Server> -o ComIbmInternalSupportManager/Java/JVM -n dump -v core. The -v core option produces a javacore (thread dump) on IBM JRE platforms (all platforms except HP and Solaris). Dump files are output to $MQSI_WORKPATH/common/errors. Note that collecting Java core dumps is invasive and will impact the performance of the Integration Server process.

The errors occur because the IBM web server Plug-in cannot locate the IBM Global Security Kit (GSKit) libraries required to initialize SSL (HTTPS). Without these libraries, the Plug-in skips the HTTPS transport and uses only HTTP. To resolve this on Linux, set the LD_LIBRARY_PATH environment variable to point to the GSKit library directory that comes with the Plug-in. For a 64-bit Plug-in v8.x, use: export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/opt/IBM/WebSphere/Plugins/gsk8/gsk8_64/lib64/. Note that simply setting this from the command line before starting the web server may not work; for RHEL Linux add the export command to /etc/sysconfig/httpd, and for SLES/SUSE Linux add it to /usr/sbin/envvars so the variable is set when the web server starts.

This information is documented in IBM Security Bulletin swg21975233. The bulletin covers CVE-2015-7575, the MD5 'SLOTH' vulnerability affecting TLS 1.2 in WebSphere Message Broker and IBM Integration Bus (versions 9.0 and 10.0 on AIX, HP-UX, Linux, Solaris, and Windows). The vulnerability allows a man-in-the-middle attacker to impersonate a TLS server and obtain credentials via a collision attack when MD5 is used to sign the ServerKeyExchange message. CVSS Base Score is 7.1. No workarounds or mitigations are listed; planned maintenance release dates are available at swg27006308. The vulnerability was reported by Karthikeyan Bhargavan at INRIA and the bulletin was originally published on 23 Jan 2016.

This error occurs when the profile version does not match the portal binary version. To resolve, update the profile to match the binary version using the UpdateProfile command. On z/OS, run: <wp_profile_root>/PortalServer/bin/UpdateProfile.sh install CF skipPreCheckProfile. On all other platforms, run: <wp_profile_root>/PortalServer/bin/UpdateProfile.bat|.sh install CF. If you performed a binary installation and created the profile later, or migrated from 6.1.x, ensure the PortalServer/wps.properties file correctly references the profile by adding ProfileName=<your profile name> if it does not exist. Also verify all profiles are at the same level before starting the upgrade.

CVSS Base Score is 4.3 with vector (CVSS:3.0/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N). All versions of WebSphere MQ 5.3 and MQ 8 for HPE NonStop Server are affected. Remediation is available via IBM Fix Central for MQ 5.3 (release 5.3.1.14) and MQ 8. No workarounds or mitigations are listed.

These are false error messages that can rarely occur on the DataPower 9235 appliance. The problem does not affect appliance operation other than the continuous failure message. First, confirm the power supplies are actually working by checking the LED status on the power supplies - if the LEDs are green, the power supplies are working normally. To recover from the false errors, perform a reboot of the appliance to reset the sensors. From the WebGUI: Control Panel → System Control → In the 'Shutdown' section choose 'Reboot System' then click 'Shutdown'. From the CLI: enter 'top', then 'shutdown reboot', then 'y'. In most cases, the reboot resets the sensors and no additional errors are logged. If the issue reoccurs on the same appliance, contact IBM DataPower support with information including how many times the issue occurred and outputs from CLI commands: show clock, show version, show ipmi, show sensors-other, config, service show, and test hardware.

To identify indexing errors in the Atlas database: 1) Login to the Atlas database as the PSSAPL user. 2) Run the query: select * from ctx_user_index_errors; 3) Copy the value in the ERR_TEXTKEY field. 4) Run the query: select * from documentlibrary where rowid='<value from Step 3>'; 5) This will list the document that has the indexing error. Note: Sometimes encrypted and password protected documents cause document indexing errors.

To remove the default compressed references and eliminate the 4GB native memory restriction on Class Pointers and Monitors/Locks, set -Xnocompressedrefs as a generic JVM argument. Be aware that this will result in a significant increase in Java heap memory requirements (it is not uncommon for 70% more heap space to be required), so you should adjust the Java heap size to a larger value and monitor/retune garbage collection as required.

When multiple versions of JDBC drivers from the same vendor are configured in WebSphere Application Server (irrespective of scope), there is a possibility of class collision and the class may be loaded from an unexpected driver jar, so the version reported in DSRA8206I may not match the jar specified in the JDBC provider. To ensure only the jar specified in the JDBC provider classpath is used for all data sources under that provider, go to the JDBC Provider settings and enable "Isolate this resource provider". Also verify that WebSphere variables such as ORACLE_JDBC_DRIVER_PATH and VMM_JDBC_CLASSPATH (stored in variables.xml at cell/node scope) are not referencing the older ojdbc14.jar.

wpcollector is a command-line tool delivered with WebSphere Portal (beginning with the 7.0 release) that automates the collection of portal logs and configuration files. It gathers profile logs (including server logs and traces), configuration files, and version information, then compresses them into a wp.mustgather-<timestamp>.zip file located in the <wp_profile_root>/filesForAutoPD/ directory for submission to IBM Support. On Windows, Unix/Linux, or IBM i, it is run via wpcollector.bat or wpcollector.sh from the PortalServer/bin directory; on z/OS, diagnostics are collected via the 'Collect Diagnostics' option in the Portal configuration panel. If tracing is required, it must be manually enabled and the problem recreated before running wpcollector.

On Solaris (SunOS), the -Xverbosegc option does not write verbose GC output to a log file by default; it writes to native_stdout. To write verbose GC output to a specified log file, add the following parameters to the generic JVM arguments: -XX:+PrintGCDetails, -XX:+PrintGCDateStamps, -XX:+PrintHeapAtGC, and -Xloggc:/tmp/gc.log (replace /tmp/gc.log with your desired file path). To enable log file rotation, additionally add: -XX:+UseGCLogFileRotation, -XX:NumberOfGCLogFiles=10, and -XX:GCLogFileSize=10M.

The behavior is controlled by the transaction timeout, not the session timeout. In the TeamServer web module deployment descriptor (WEB-INF/web.xml), the property ilog.rules.teamserver.transaction.timeout is set to 600 seconds (10 minutes) by default. If a transactional operation performed by RTS/DC takes longer than this timeout to complete, the transaction is rolled back and the operation is not completed, which can cause users to be kicked out while actively authoring rules. You can increase this value in the web.xml file of the RTS/DC EAR (jrules-teamserver-<appserver>.ear\teamserver.war\WEB-INF). Additionally, check application server specific container-level transaction timeouts (for example, in WebSphere Application Server check the 'Maximum transaction timeout' and increase it as needed).

Beginning in firmware version 6.0 and above, the default SSL settings changed: Crypto profiles now enable TLSv1.2 and TLSv1.1 by default. This affects the protocol version included in the Client Hello when DataPower acts as the SSL client. Some legacy servers with non-compliant SSL implementations reject connection attempts when TLSv1.2 or TLSv1.1 are used, causing the handshake to fail without negotiating to a mutually agreeable protocol. To resolve, upgrade the SSL server to a compliant version, or disable TLSv1.2 and TLSv1.1 within the Crypto Profile (navigate to Objects > Crypto Configuration > Crypto Profile, select the specific profile, and adjust the supported SSL protocol versions in the Options selection).

When there is a "-" in a string you are searching for, you need to use "\" in front of the "-". For example, "String1-String2" should be searched as "String1\-String2". Please refer to the Oracle documentation for Special Characters in Oracle Text Queries for other reserved characters.

As a local fix, open the WAS admin console, navigate to Resources > Resource environment providers > WP ScriptingService > Custom properties, delete the entry named "ServerExt.applications" with value "com.ibm.wps.scripting.server.ApplicationServerExtensions", save, and restart the server.

In a clustered environment, the latest ruleset may not execute if the hot deployment notification was not sent by the RES console or not received by all Execution Units (XU) via JMX. Verify that the user publishing the update has sufficient administrative rights (Monitor role in WebSphere Application Server) to notify all Execution Units. Additionally, if the updated ruleset cannot be parsed successfully, RES falls back to an earlier active version that parses. If asynchronous ruleset parsing is enabled, an earlier version may be used while the updated ruleset is being parsed. Also confirm the requested ruleset path is correct (a path without version requests the highest version).

IBM Integration Bus Hypervisor Edition V9.0 and WebSphere Message Broker Hypervisor Edition V8.0 ship with versions of Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL) Server that are vulnerable to CVE-2011-5320, CVE-2017-15670, CVE-2017-15671, and CVE-2017-15804. IBM Security Bulletin swg22012983 (CVE-2018-1371) describes that an IBM MQ client connecting to an MQ queue manager can cause a SIGSEGV in the queue manager's amqrmppa channel process, terminating it. According to the security bulletin, multiple vulnerabilities exist in the IBM® SDK Java™ Technology Edition that is shipped with IBM WebSphere Application Server, which in turn ships with WebSphere Enterprise Service Bus. This means the Java SDK vulnerabilities directly affect WebSphere Application Server, and because WebSphere Enterprise Service Bus includes/ships with that version of WebSphere Application Server, the vulnerabilities also affect WebSphere Enterprise Service Bus versions 6.2, 7.0, and 7.5. Specifically for CVE-2015-2613: it is an unspecified vulnerability in the Java SE Embedded JCE component that could allow a remote attacker to obtain sensitive information (CVSS Base Score: 5, Vector: AV:N/AC:L/Au:N/C:P/I:N/A:N). Remediation details and fixes are provided in the related bulletin for WebSphere Application Server July 2015 CPU (swg21962931).

Yes, the ITCAM Monitoring Agent for Microsoft SQL Server supports SQL Server 2017. Support was added in version 6.3.1.13 (Interim Fix 0001, 6.3.1.13-TIV-ITM_SQL-IF0001) as documented under DEFECT 171127: 'Add tolerance support for SQL Server 2017. Added support for SQL Server 2017 version.'

The error is related to the Windows FIPS security policy and/or missing key file distribution. First, verify that the Local Security Policy 'System Cryptography: Use FIPS compliant algorithms for encryption, hashing and signing' is set to Disabled (Administrative Tools > Local Security Policy > Local Policies > Security Options). If the policy is already disabled or the error persists, ensure the encryption key file (dc_ktf.xml) has been properly exported from the server and distributed/imported to the client folder on the Windows 10 machine; without this file the FIPS key information cannot be located and parameters cannot be validated.

The 'Too many open files' error indicates the Portal process has exhausted its file handle limit (which includes sockets), typically caused by system configuration limits being too low or file descriptor leaks in the application. To resolve: increase the ulimit for file handles using 'ulimit -n [value]' (setting to 8000 is usually sufficient for normal runtime), then restart the application server and nodeagent on the same command line where the ulimit was executed. If errors persist with a high limit, check for file descriptor leaks by monitoring open files with 'lsof -p [PID] -r [interval]' on AIX/Linux or capture a Javacore using 'kill -3 PID' to verify the NOFILE limit.
The S-TAP Approval Needed option is likely checked in the S-TAP Certification screen on the Appliance. Uncheck the Approval box and the S-TAPs should start connecting.

Yes. By default, when an SCA module is uninstalled (including during an update), its associated destinations are removed even if there are still messages in the destination queue, so messages residing on internal SCA queues would be deleted. To prevent this and preserve the SCA destinations (and their messages), set the SCA.recycleDestinations custom JVM property for the module to false.

The HTTP Session time-out for a Workplace application on WebSphere Application Server can be set in five locations, with the following precedence from lowest to highest: (1) Server Level via Administrative Console (Servers > Application Servers > Your Server > Web Container > Session Management); (2) Enterprise Application Level via Administrative Console (Applications > Enterprise Applications > Your Application > Session Management) with Override selected, which overrides the Server Level; (3) Web Application Level via Administrative Console (Applications > Enterprise Applications > Your Application > Web Module > Your Web App.war > Session Management) with Override selected, which overrides Server and Enterprise Application settings; (4) Application packaging level stored in web.xml as <session-config><session-timeout>value</session-timeout></session-config>, which overrides all Administrative Console settings; and (5) Application code using the setMaxInactiveInterval() method on the HttpSession object, which overrides all other settings. To increase the time-out, set the desired value in minutes at the appropriate level, ensuring Override is checked at Enterprise or Web Application levels if overriding parent settings.

The information is published in IBM Security Bulletin swg21959745, titled 'Vulnerability in Diffie-Hellman ciphers affects IBM WebSphere MQ Internet Passthru (CVE-2015-4000)'. The bulletin describes the Logjam attack (CVE-2015-4000) where TLS connections using Diffie-Hellman key exchange can be downgraded to 512-bit export-grade ciphers via man-in-the-middle techniques, allowing attackers to recover session keys and modify traffic. It affects all versions of IBM WebSphere MQ Internet Pass-thru (MQIPT) prior to 2.1.0.2. The CVSS Base Score is 4.3. Remediation requires upgrading to MQIPT 2.1.0.2 (available via SupportPac MS81). No workarounds are available.

The 2999 ms delay comes from the Work Load Manager messaging-engine lookup wait controlled by the sib.trm.linger property. Tune sib.trm.linger in the sib.properties file to change the messaging engine lookup delay (the default wait is about 3 seconds). Set it under <WAS_HOME>/properties (applies to all profiles) or <PROFILE_ROOT>/properties (applies to all servers in that profile; this takes precedence if defined in both). After changing the property, restart the server. Note: the technote specifically recommends increasing sib.trm.linger above 3 only when the HA manager cannot locate a running messaging engine within three seconds (check SystemOut.log for hung threads / CWSID0016I messaging engine state); lowering it is the lever for reducing the WaitForWLMDat sleep when writing to a remote queue.

This information is documented in IBM Security Bulletin swg21985013. The bulletin states that IBM Integration Bus (IIB) V9 and WebSphere Message Broker (WMB) V8, upon installation on Unix platforms, set incorrect permissions for an object (the isadc directory), which could allow a local attacker to manipulate certain files (CVE-2016-0394, CVSS Base Score 4.0). Remediation is available via APAR IT14845 in IIB Fix Pack 9.0.0.6 and WMB Fix Pack 8.0.0.8. As a workaround on Unix platforms, run: find <IIB install dir>/isadc -type d -exec chmod 755 {} \; ; find <IIB install dir>/isadc -type f -exec chmod 644 {} \; ; find <IIB install dir>/isadc -type f -name *.sh -print -exec chmod 755. For unsupported versions, upgrade to a fixed supported version.

No. IBM Mobile Foundation, IBM Worklight, IBM Worklight Foundation, and IBM MobileFirst Platform Foundation support Oracle JDK 7 but do not support Oracle JDK 8. Because Oracle's auto-update feature may automatically migrate you from JDK 7 to JDK 8 on Windows and Mac OS, you should not upgrade to Oracle JDK 8. If you have already migrated, you must revert to Oracle JDK 7 by uninstalling JDK 8 and reinstalling the latest version of Oracle JDK 7.

The resolver uses a digest to cache URLs (such as resource aggregator collections), and this digest remains the same between server restarts. Because the digest does not change, theme files continue to be served from the browser or proxy cache (HTTP 304) rather than being loaded from the server, so updated graphics are not displayed until the cache is manually cleared (e.g., Ctrl+F5). To force the updated theme resources to load, set the "digest.seed" key in the WP ConfigService to any string value; this generates a new digest on server boot and changes the URLs so the updated resources are fetched from the server.

Yes. To prevent internal SCA destinations (queues) from being deleted and recreated when uninstalling, reinstalling, or updating an SCA module, set the custom JVM property SCA.recycleDestinations to false for the module. This preserves the SCA destinations and any messages they contain.

In CMOD v9.0 on Windows, server trace files are written in binary format and must be converted using the ARSTFMT command located in the CMOD\9.0\bin directory. Open a command prompt, navigate to the CMOD\9.0\bin directory, and run: arstfmt -i C:\Users\IBM_ADMIN\path\to\file -o C:\Users\IBM_ADMIN\path\to\file\name.txt, where the -i parameter specifies the unreadable binary trace file and the -o parameter specifies the name of the formatted output text file.

This is expected behavior due to Defect 138519. In this fix pack, the default instance of SQL Server is now identified as 'MSSQLSERVER' instead of the hostname. This change was made because in environments where there was both a default instance and a named instance having the same name as the hostname, there were configuration issues. To resolve this, you need to unconfigure the instance previously configured with the hostname name and reconfigure it using the name 'MSSQLSERVER'. Steps: 1) Open Manage Tivoli Enterprise Monitoring Services (MTEMS), 2) Right-click the template row and select 'Configure Using Defaults', 3) Select the default instance with name HOSTNAME from 'Server To Monitor' and click '>>' to unconfigure it, 4) Select the instance named 'MSSQLSERVER' in 'Database Servers Available' and click '<<' to configure it, 5) Set configuration parameters and start the agent.

After a period of inactivity (such as a day or two), the underlying network connection for the data source may become invalid even though the data source remains active from the WebSphere Application Server connection pool perspective. A typical cause is a firewall between the Application Server and the Database that has a policy to discard network connections that remain idle for some time, which can result in connection failures when the application attempts to use the connection again.

The clearing event is not received because the EIF probe on the OMNIbus side is resetting/closing (<RST>) the TCP/IP connection after receiving the event, causing the event to be dropped before it appears in the EIF logs or OMNIbus. To resolve this, change the ConnectionMode in the om_tec.config file on the ITM Server (TEMS) from 'ConnectionMode=co' (connection oriented) to 'ConnectionMode=connection_less', then restart the EIF using 'tacmd refreshTECinfo -t eif'.

According to the supported operating system matrix, Apple Macintosh OSX Mavericks (10.9) only supports IBM SPSS Statistics 22 and IBM SPSS Statistics 23. If you are attempting to install IBM SPSS Statistics Subscription (a newer release), it is not supported on OS X 10.9.5. You would need to upgrade your Mac OS to a newer version (such as OS X 10.10 Yosemite or later) to install newer SPSS Statistics releases, or use Statistics 22 or 23 on OS X 10.9. Note that for Statistics 22 on OS X 10.9, you must install Apple Java SE 6 (1.6.0_65) first before installing Statistics 22.

According to the retrieved technote, for FileNet P8 repositories case insensitive searches can be performed by setting the 'Force Case Insensitive Search' flag on the object store. Since this flag has already been checked, the documented alternative is to write a request filter that changes the case of the query to all upper or all lower case.

The error IQQG0205E indicates a version incompatibility between the IBM Content Search Services client embedded in the IBM FileNet Content Platform Engine and the IBM Content Search Services server. The client version must match the server version. Check the readme files for your installed IBM FileNet Content Platform Engine and IBM FileNet Content Search Services fix packs to verify fix pack requirements and ensure the client files included in the Content Platform Engine match the Content Search Services server version.

This is a known DB2 11 for z/OS issue documented in APAR PI19804. SQLCODE -401 (DSNT408I) with SQLERRP=DSNXOBFC occurs during CREATE PROCEDURE for a native SQL procedure when a control statement contains an IN-LIST predicate that references SQL variables (e.g., IF var IN (sqlvar1, sqlvar2)). DB2 does not process the SQL variables in the IN-LIST predicate properly, resulting in the incorrect SQLCODE -401. The stored procedure CIUSNTSR created by CICS IA CIUDBCQ JCL contains such a construct. Apply the PTF for APAR PI19804 (UI20622) to correct the processing of SQL variables in IN-LIST predicates.

This crash is a known side effect of applying interim fix PI50993. According to the technote, after applying this fix, the API in HTTPCore and HTTPClient libraries are no longer visible to applications, which results in NoClassDefFoundError (or VerifyError for inaccessible classes like org/apache/http/HttpEntity). To resolve this error, the application must be updated to bundle the HTTPCore and HTTPClient libraries with the application itself.

This information is documented in IBM Security Bulletin swg21985017. The bulletin covers CVE-2016-2961, where IBM Integration Bus uses Apache Tomcat for HTTPInput and SOAPInput nodes, and an unauthenticated remote attacker can send a malformed HTTP POST request to the integration server HTTP listener to obtain a Java stack trace revealing the Apache Tomcat version. CVSS Base Score is 5.3 (Vector: CVSS:3.0/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N). Affected products are IBM Integration Bus V10.0 and V9.0, and WebSphere Message Broker V8.0. Remediation is via APAR IT15188: available in fix pack 10.0.0.5 for IIB V10, interim fix from IBM Fix Central for IIB V9, targeted for fix pack 9.0.0.6; interim fix from IBM Fix Central for WMB V8, targeted for fix pack 8.0.0.8. For unsupported versions, upgrade to a fixed supported version is recommended.

The StoredIQ Dataserver login page may not appear in the browser due to a missing or incorrect hostname in the /etc/hosts file. To resolve this: 1) Login to the appliance as root, 2) Edit the /etc/hosts file, 3) Update the correct hostname and save the changes, and 4) Restart the appliance.

Yes, you can switch IBM Business Process Choreographer Explorer (BPC Explorer) from HTTPS back to HTTP using the unsecureExplorer.ant script. This information is documented in IBM Security Bulletin swg22013088. The bulletin states that IBM API Connect is affected by CVE-2016-1000232, where the Node.js tough-cookie module is vulnerable to a denial of service caused by a regular expression error. A remote attacker could exploit this by sending a sufficiently large HTTP request Cookie header, causing the application to consume an overly large amount of CPU resources. The CVSS Base Score is 5.3 (CVSS Vector: CVSS:3.0/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:L). Affected versions include IBM API Connect 5.0.6.0-5.0.6.5, 5.0.7.0-5.0.7.2, and 5.0.8.0. The vulnerability is addressed in IBM API Connect V5.0.6.6 (for 5.0.0.0-5.0.6.5) and V5.0.8.1 (for 5.0.7.0-5.0.7.2 and 5.0.8.0) via APAR LI79986. Fixes can be obtained from IBM Fix Central by selecting the 'APIConnect_Management' package for the relevant release.

Use the WASServiceHelper utility (shipped with WebSphere Application Server v8 and later in the bin directory, replacing WASServiceCmd) to create a Windows service for the Deployment Manager profile. The service is created using WASService.exe with parameters such as -add, -serverName "dmgr", -profilePath pointing to your Dmgr profile directory, -logRoot, -logFile, -startType (e.g., automatic or manual), and -restart options. Example command structure from the technote: WASService.exe -add "Deployment Mgr01" -serverName "dmgr" -profilePath "C:\Program Files\IBM\WebSphere\AppServer\profiles\Dmgr01" -logRoot "C:\Program Files\IBM\WebSphere\AppServer\profiles\Dmgr01\logs\dmgr" -logFile "C:\Program Files\IBM\WebSphere\AppServer\profiles\Dmgr01\logs\dmgr\WS_startdmgr.log" -encodeParams -stopArgs "-username <user> -password ******" -startType manual -restart false. This creates an entry in WASServiceCmd.log showing the actual command used. For BPM 8.5 (based on WAS 8.5.5), use WASServiceHelper.bat in the profile's bin directory to create the Windows service for the dmgr and node profiles so they run independently of the logged-in admin user.

In a clustered environment, the WIMSYSTEM.ear must be installed on the Deployment Manager (DMGR). If the .ear was originally installed on a non-DMGR node (such as the WebSphere_Portal server), subsequent attempts to install it on the DMGR will appear to succeed, but the wp-add-property task will continue to fail with the 'Can not find EJB' error. To resolve: 1) Uninstall the WIMSYSTEM enterprise application from the WebSphere_Portal server using the WebSphere Administrative console. 2) Install the .ear file on the DMGR following the steps in Document #1358381. 3) Verify in the serverindex.xml files that the DMGR server entry contains references to WIMSYSTEM.ear in its deployedApplications, while the application server entry does not.

You can check if a table was created as NOT LOGGED INITIALLY (NLI) using either of these methods:

1) Using db2cat:
   db2cat -db <dbname> -n <TableName> -s <Schema> -t | grep "Table not logged"
   - If the output shows 'Table not logged : 0', the table was NOT created as NLI.
   - If it returns '1', the table WAS created as NLI.

2) Using db2look to get the DDL:
   db2look -d <database_name> -t <table_name> -e -o <output_file_name.out>
   The DDL output will show if the table was created with "NOT LOGGED INITIALLY".

Note: ALTER TABLE ... ACTIVATE NOT LOGGED INITIALLY will not appear in these commands, as it only activates NLI for the current unit of work. Also, starting from DB2 V9, the LOG_ATTRIBUTE column in SYSCAT.TABLES is no longer used (always 0) and cannot be used to check this.

This issue occurs because Internet Explorer 8 and later includes its own version of Data Execution Prevention (DEP), which can cause the browser to freeze or stop during remote scanning. To resolve this, disable DEP in Internet Explorer: 1) Open the Tools menu and select Internet Options, 2) Select the Advanced tab, 3) Uncheck 'Enable memory protection to mitigate online attacks', 4) Close all windows, restart the browser, and start scanning again. Note: If using Datacap 8.1, this issue has been fixed in 8.1 Fix Pack 1.

This information is documented in IBM Security Bulletin swg21962588. The bulletin covers multiple vulnerabilities in IBM SDK Java Technology Edition Version 6 and 7 used by IBM OS Images for Red Hat Linux Systems and AIX, disclosed in the January 2015 IBM Java SDK updates. CVE-2015-0410 is an unspecified vulnerability in the Security component allowing a remote attacker to cause denial of service (CVSS Base Score 5, Vector AV:N/AC:L/Au:N/C:N/I:N/A:P). CVE-2014-6593 is an unspecified vulnerability in the JSSE component with partial confidentiality and integrity impact (CVSS Base Score 4, Vector AV:N/AC:H/Au:N/C:P/I:P/A:N). Affected products are IBM OS Image for Red Hat Linux Systems 2.0.0.1 and earlier, and IBM OS Image for AIX 2.0.0.1 and earlier. Remediation requires applying the Java Update for Linux (fix ID Java_Update_Linux_2) and Java Update for AIX (fix ID Java_Update_AIX_2) from IBM Fix Central, importing the fix into the Emergency Fix catalogue, applying it to deployed virtual machines (upgrading to IBM Java JDK 7.0 SR8 FP10 interim fix and IBM Java JDK 6.0 SR16 FP3 interim fix), and restarting the instances. No workarounds or mitigations are available.

To configure the Data Power Agent to use TLSv1.2, manually set the configuration item KBN_SOMA_PROTOCOL to TLSv1.2. On Windows platforms, this item is located in the KBNENV and KBNENV_<instanceName> files. After modifying the value, the agent instance must be restarted to enable the change. Additionally, when the instance is re-configured, the value of KBN_SOMA_PROTOCOL in KBNENV_<instanceName> will be updated to match the value set in KBNENV.

Yes, you can run different levels of the RDz host and client. The retrieved Technotes do not describe a direct OutOfMemoryError fix (e.g., heap sizing); they address the related memory pressure from very large Decision Warehouse traces. Because each EXECUTION_TRACES.FULL_EXECUTION_TRACE record can be several MB, reduce the persisted DW trace used by the Scenario Suite Provider (SSP) when running DVS scenario suites: customize the SSP trace to filter out information not needed in the DW (the provided sample removes all rules that did not fire), which keeps the persisted trace small even with many rules/scenarios. Note only the DW-persisted trace is reduced; the original larger trace is still used by DVS for the tests. Implementation per swg21438208: unjar jrules-ssptrace-src.jar, edit ./jrules-ssptrace/build.xml properties (jrules.home, sspInput, sspOutput), run 'ant repackage-ssp', and deploy the customized SSP at the sspOutput path. Separately, swg21433278 notes trace-persistence failures can be silent and that logging the full execution trace XML at FINEST can itself emit several MB, so avoid enabling that level when memory is constrained.

SQLCODE=-1585, SQLSTATE=54048 occurs because the DB2 instance does not have all 4 sizes of temporary tablespaces defined. The database administrator must ensure that System Temp tablespaces exist for all four page sizes: 4k, 8k, 16k, and 32k. These must be configured as System Temp tablespaces, not User Temp tablespaces. If only some sizes (for example, only 8k and 32k) were manually created, the database-transfer task will fail with this error while gathering data from the source database.

To use ITDS 6.3 on RHEL 6, you must install the Tivoli Directory Server 6.3 General Availability (GA) version using native operating system utilities (such as rpm/yum) only, and then upgrade to fix pack 10. GUI tools such as the Instance Administration tool (idsxinst) and Configuration tool (idsxcfg) are not supported on RHEL 6; use the appropriate command-line tools instead.

This occurs because of a code change introduced in DB2 V10.1 GA: the off-line backup command can be blocked for a short period of time while a connect database command is being executed, even when the database is quiesced. This behavior did not exist in V9.7. When other users (with only connect privilege) are repeatedly attempting to connect to the quiesced database, they receive SQL20157N, and the concurrent off-line backup attempt can fail as a result of this blocking. To avoid this, use the quiesce instance command with the restricted access option instead of quiesce database, or retry the off-line backup command if the error occurs.

When removing a CHLAUTH record with ACTION(REMOVE), you must specify all attributes that uniquely identify the specific record you want to delete. In your case, since there are two records for BMMADMIN.SVRCONN differing by ADDRESS, you must include the ADDRESS attribute in the REMOVE command to target the correct one. Also note that USERSRC is not a valid parameter for ACTION(REMOVE) (it is only valid for ADD/REPLACE). Use: SET CHLAUTH(BMMADMIN.SVRCONN) TYPE(USERMAP) ADDRESS(<IP_ADDRESS>) ACTION(REMOVE). If the record also has a CLNTUSER attribute, include it with single quotes (e.g., CLNTUSER('value')).

This is a known limitation of the Filter Analyzer in Netcool/Impact when comparing two ObjectServer fields against each other or a field against GetDate within an EventReader Filter. To resolve, add the property 'impact.[EventReaderName].consolidatefilters=false' (where [EventReaderName] is the lower-case name of the EventReader, e.g., omnibuseventreader) to the EventReader properties file located at $NCHOME/impact/etc/[ImpactServerName]_[EventReaderName].props (where [ImpactServerName] is the ImpactServer name, NCI by default). An ImpactServer restart is required to enable the property. In a clustered environment, stop Secondary ImpactServers first, then stop and restart the Primary, then restart the Secondaries to ensure the property is distributed and not overwritten. Note that this issue only affects the Filter Analyzer and does not impact the EventReader's ability to parse the Filter.

This error occurs on IBM DB2 when the maxpropvalue property 'mxe.db.format.nullvalue' is incorrectly set to 'ISNULL' (the SQL Server value) instead of 'COALESCE' (required for DB2). To resolve: 1) Make sure MXServer is stopped. 2) Connect to the database backend and run: update maximo.maxpropvalue set propvalue='COALESCE' where propname='mxe.db.format.nullvalue'; 3) Start MXServer again. For DB2 the value must be COALESCE and cannot be changed to another value; ISNULL is only for SQL Server, NVL is for Oracle.

Best practices for working with IBM BPM Support include: (1) Gather MustGather data before contacting support to expedite troubleshooting, including environment description (BPM product/version via versionInfo commands, OS, database, topology), complete log directories (install_root/profiles/profile_name/logs/server_name and .../logs/ffdc), and configuration files such as TeamWorksConfiguration.running.xml from the process-center or process-server directories. (2) Provide screenshots if error messages are not visible in logs. (3) Supply a simplified, isolated test case without external dependencies, including .twx exports from Process Designer, Project Interchange (PI) and EAR files for Advanced Integration Services if applicable, and exact reproduction steps with timestamps. (4) Describe business impact including deadlines and customer effects. (5) Review SystemOut.log for errors around the issue timestamp. (6) Use the bpmdc command to compress logs into a .zip, set appropriate trace strings via administrative console or wsadmin to recreate the issue, then run bpmdc again to collect logs. (7) After opening a PMR, use bpmdc-PMR=PMRnumber-uploadToIBM=yes to upload data directly to IBM.

AMQ9716 occurs because, starting with WebSphere MQ 7.0.1.0, OCSP certificate revocation checking is enabled by default. Your SSL certificates likely contain an OCSP AuthorityInfoAccess (AIA) extension pointing to an OCSP responder (or CRL distribution point). If the queue manager or client cannot contact the server(s) listed in the AIA, the revocation status returns UNKNOWN, and by default MQ blocks the channel from starting and reports AMQ9716. To resolve, first verify that the URL in the certificate's AIA extension is reachable from the MQ server/client. As a temporary workaround, set OCSPAuthentication=OPTIONAL in the SSL stanza of qm.ini (UNIX/Linux) or via 'amqmdain reg YourQMgrName -c add -s SSL -v OCSPAuthentication=OPTIONAL' (Windows) for a queue manager, or in the client ini file (e.g., mqclient.ini) for clients; then issue REFRESH SECURITY TYPE(SSL) on the queue manager or restart the client application. Once the underlying connectivity issue is fixed, re-enable OCSP enforcement for security.

When a queue full event occurs, WebSphere MQ disables the event. In a clustered environment, the most likely cause is that the hot deployment notification was not received by all Execution Units (XU), or there is a permission issue preventing the notification from being sent. Validate that the user publishing the ruleset update has sufficient administrative rights (Monitor role in WebSphere Application Server) so the deployment can notify all Execution Units through JMX. Also verify that all cluster nodes are within the same WebSphere Application Server Cell (or JBoss/WebLogic domain), as the RES notification mechanism only works within one cell by design. Since direct calls to the application server execute the correct version but the HTTP service layer does not, confirm that the Execution Unit serving the HTTP service has received the hot deploy notification and is not falling back to a cached earlier version due to a parsing failure or missed notification.

With the introduction of Managed Pages in WebSphere Portal 8.0, virtual portal deletions require more transaction time when removing the virtual portal from the system. This increased transaction time can exceed the default 120-second transaction timeout (the total and/or maximum transaction lifetime timeout value(s) for the server, or the WCM component's transaction timeout), causing the WTRN0006W timeout and the delete operation to fail. To resolve, increase the total transaction lifetime timeout and maximum transaction timeout values (for example, to 600 seconds or greater).

This is a known behavior/limitation that occurs when two versions of Data Studio (3.1.1 and 4.1.2) are installed on the same machine. When the SQL Server database is restarted after Microsoft patching, the connections cached in the WebSphere Application Server connection pool become invalid. When the application attempts to use these pooled connections, the database vendor issues an exception indicating the connection is no longer valid, resulting in a com.ibm.websphere.ce.cm.StaleConnectionException. If the application does not handle this exception with proper retry logic, the appserver can become unresponsive. To prevent this, configure the data source connection pool by setting Minimum connections to 0 and setting Unused timeout and Reap timeout values so their sum does not exceed any network-level idle connection timeout, or purge the connection pool to discard the stale cached connections and allow the pool to refill with new valid connections.

After upgrading from WebSphere Application Server V7.0 to V8.5, the default behavior for the user identifier passed to the MQ queue manager changed. In V7.0 (and V8.0), when no authentication alias or credentials are supplied, a blank user identifier is passed to MQ, causing MQ to authorize based on the listener's userid (typically 'mqm' or 'MUSR_MQADMIN'). In V8.5, a non-blank user identifier is passed by default. If this user is not known on the queue manager server, is not authorized to connect, or exceeds 12 characters (causing truncation), MQ returns reason code 2035 (MQRC_NOT_AUTHORIZED). To resolve, configure an authentication alias with valid MQ credentials in the connection factory, or ensure the user identifier being passed is authorized on the queue manager.

The error occurs because the profilePath directory already exists. When creating a profile using BPMConfig with the -profilePath parameter, the specified profile path must not exist. Ensure that the parent directory of the profile path exists and that the user has write privileges to create a new directory, but do not create the profile path directory itself. For example, if you want to create a profile under /usr/BPM850profiles/myProfile, create the /usr/BPM850profiles directory, but do not create the /usr/BPM850profiles/myProfile directory.

The JMSListener autoreconnect properties are likely configured incorrectly. In the file $NCHOME/impact/etc/[ImpactServerName]_[JMSListenerName].props, the properties must be set WITHOUT the additional '.jms' bit. Use: impact.[JMSListenerName].autoreconnect=true and impact.[JMSListenerName].autoreconnect.pollinterval=[TimeValue] (where [TimeValue] is in milliseconds, e.g., 30000 for 30 seconds). Do NOT use impact.[JMSListenerName].jms.autoreconnect=true. After correcting the properties, restart the Impact server for the changes to take effect.

The Monitoring agent for MySQL does not collect data for some attribute groups (Statistics, Availability, Operations per second, MySQL status data, Session status, Agent Configuration, Global status, Global variables, Server String properties, Numeric properties) when monitoring MySQL server versions 5.7.6 and above because certain INFORMATION_SCHEMA tables used by the agent are deprecated in these versions. This causes a java.sql.SQLException: The 'INFORMATION_SCHEMA.GLOBAL_STATUS' feature is disabled; see the documentation for 'show_compatibility_56' in the JDBC trace logs. To resolve this, set the system variable show_compatibility_56=ON. This can be done from the MySQL command prompt using: set global show_compatibility_56=ON; or by adding show_compatibility_56=ON to the my.cnf configuration file (located at <MySQL_Installation_Dir>/my.cnf for Windows and /etc/my.cnf for UNIX/Linux), which requires a MySQL server restart. Note that the default value is ON for MySQL versions <=5.7.7 and OFF for versions >=5.7.8. You can check the current value by running: show global variables like "show_compatibility_56";

No, exact PVU consumption cannot be viewed per virtual machine. Per PVU and RVU MAPC subcapacity license terms, license consumption is specified only at the physical server level; PVU/RVU MAPC values cannot be calculated or presented on the VM or LPAR level, and License Metric Tool / BigFix Inventory does not provide such per-VM data. To check your licensed PVU usage, look at the physical server level: in the All IBM Metrics / IBM PVU subcapacity reports, the second level (click the product name) shows the physical server with the 'PVU Subcapacity Limit' (column M in the audit snapshot CSV, 'Physical Server PVU Subcapacity'). Do not sum column M across rows, because the value is repeated for each VM row but refers to the single physical server. In your case the relevant subcapacity figure is the 480 PVU shown at the physical server level, not a per-VM breakdown.

The issue occurs because when a .csv document is created through WorkplaceXT, the mime type is set to "text/csv" instead of "application/vnd.ms-excel" (which is the mime type set when creating the same document through ACCE). To resolve this, add a mime-mapping section to the web.xml file mapping the csv extension to the application/vnd.ms-excel mime type:

<mime-mapping>
  <extension>csv</extension>

Based on the technote, if you cannot enter your license code in the License Authorization Wizard on your new MacBook due to an administrator privileges warning, perform the following steps for SPSS Statistics Release 24:

1. If open, close the IBM SPSS Statistics product.
2. If open, close the License Authorization Wizard.
3. Open Finder, select the 'Go' menu, select 'Utilities', and open the 'Terminal' program.
4. Type (copy/paste) the following command:
   cd /Applications/IBM/SPSS/Statistics/
5. Press Enter/Return.
6. Type (copy/paste) the following command:
   sudo chown -R root:admin 24
7. Press Enter/Return.
8. Close Terminal.
9. Launch the License Authorization Wizard.
10. The warning message should no longer appear, and you can then license your IBM SPSS Statistics product.

Note: The retrieved documentation does not provide specific steps for deactivating the license on your old MacBook; it addresses resolving the License Authorization Wizard blocker on the new machine.

The failure occurs because two Product installs used different JVM versions, causing the Deployment Engine (DE) directory to be created with different names: one using the FQDN (e.g., /home/nc_admin/.acsi_<Fully Qualified hostname>) and one using just the hostname (e.g., /home/nc_admin/.acsi_<hostname>). To resolve: 1) Ensure the current upgrade uses the same JVM version as the original install, OR 2) Remove the newly created invalid DE directory and create a soft link to the existing valid DE: backup <DE_HOME>/.acsi_<FQDN>, move <DE_HOME>/.acsi_<hostname> to a backup location, then run 'cd <DE_HOME>' and 'ln -s <DE_HOME>/.acsi_<FQDN> .acsi_<hostname>' to create the link. Confirm with 'ls -lart' showing the symlink. 3) Retry the Product install after confirming no required cleanup is needed.

The bulletin addresses CVE-2014-8917, a cross-site scripting vulnerability in IBM Dojo Toolkit caused by improper validation of user-supplied input, which affects IBM Image Construction and Composition Tool. CVSS Base Score is 4.3 with vector (AV:N/AC:M/Au:N/C:N/I:P/A:N). Affected versions are IBM Image Construction and Composition Tool v2.2.1.3, v2.3.1.0, and v2.3.2.0. Remediation requires applying specific efixes: ICCT_efix_Repository_2.2.1.3-28 for v2.2.1.3, ICCT_efix_Repository_2.3.1.0-38 for v2.3.1.0, and ICCT_efix_Repository_2.3.2.0-12 for v2.3.2.0, available via IBM Fix Central. No workarounds or mitigations are available. The bulletin was originally published on 17 June 2015.
